quotes.citation: ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཉི་ཤུ་ལྔ་པ། (Kangyur, ཉི་ཁྲི་ vol. ཀ) — the Buddha's answer on the purified Dharma eye.
quotes.why: The sūtra passage the paragraph abbreviates, in the canonical Pañcaviṃśati: by the Dharma eye the bodhisattva knows 'this person is a faith-follower, this one a Dharma-follower'. Found by own search of the Kangyur.

quotes.citation: ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཉི་ཤུ་ལྔ་པ། — the same answer, continued past the śrāvaka persons to bodhisattvas.
quotes.why: The sūtra's Dharma eye does not stop at the śrāvaka āryas the paragraph quotes: it goes on to know bodhisattvas, including one who has only just generated the mind, as irreversible or not. Found by own search of the Kangyur.

quotes.citation: ཉི་ཁྲི་ལེའུ་བརྒྱད་མ། པོད་དང་པོ། — the Dharma-eye question and answer.
quotes.why: The eight-chapter recension of the Pañcaviṃśati, whose wording (ཤཱ་རིའི་བུ, རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་བའོ) is the one the yig cha actually reproduces, rather than the Kangyur's རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ.
The root-verse lemma: the five eyes are the seventh of the ten instructions, the topic under which this whole five-eye section sits.
The verse immediately after the ten instructions opens the twenty saṅgha with exactly the typology the Dharma eye surveys: dull and sharp faculties, faith-follower and the rest.
The words the paragraph cites with ཞེས་གསུངས are Haribhadra's gloss, not the Ornament's: the Dharma eye is the subject that comprehends all ārya persons.
Ārya Vimuktisena, Haribhadra's source, puts it with a genitive: the object of the Dharma eye is the realization of all ārya persons.
A different Indian gloss: the Dharma eye is the nine powers other than knowing what is and is not possible — the gloss Tsongkhapa and Jamyang Zhepa both report.

Damṣṭrasena's line-by-line reading of the same sūtra: the Dharma eye knows śrāvaka āryas' abandonments and grounds and also bodhisattvas' conduct and powers; the faith-follower is a dull-faculty ārya śrāvaka.
Tsongkhapa pairs Haribhadra's gloss with the same sūtra line the paragraph pairs it with, and adds the word the paragraph leaves implicit: the sharp and dull faculties of ārya persons.
Tsongkhapa reporting a 'Great Commentary' that makes the Dharma eye unobstructed entry into the twelve branches of scripture — a scriptural rather than a person-knowing eye.
Gyaltsab Je's gloss, which the yig cha's own definition follows almost word for word.
Gyaltsab Je's boundary: the Dharma eye from the subsequent attainment of the path of seeing — which Chökyi Gyaltsen quotes and then qualifies.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's own definition, given a page later in the analytical part of this same section: what this paragraph glosses, turned into a definition.
The objection the yig cha records against its own definition: other things are called 'Dharma eye' — the uninterrupted path of seeing, and a 'scriptural' Dharma eye.
Chökyi Gyaltsen: Gyaltsab's boundaries mark where each eye is chiefly obtained, not where it first occurs; śrāvakas too have the Dharma eye.
The reason: a śrāvaka with the clairvoyance that knows others' minds knows the gradation of ārya faculties, and so satisfies the definition.

quotes.citation: ཕར་ཕྱིན་མཐའ་དཔྱོད་རིན་ཆེན་སྒྲོན་མེ། སྤྱན་ལྔ། ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། (རྟོབ is the file's OCR for རྟོགས)
quotes.why: Jamyang Zhepa's Gomang definition widens the object to the faculties of ordinary beings and āryas alike and grounds it in the union of calm abiding and insight.
Panchen Sonam Drakpa (Loseling) keeps the ārya-faculties reading, as the yig cha does.
